newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Physical cocoa still hampered by strong sterling.
newsitem.headline: Physical cocoa still hampered by strong sterling.

text.p: A fresh slide cocoa futures this week sparked some activity in Europe's physical market but trade levels in general remained hampered by the strong pound.
Traders said industry buyers were in the market earlier in the week for both beans and products although demand soon dried up when currency factors came into play.
"The higher sterling rate is killing off quite a lot of the physical business," one trader said. "Industry is coming in for bits and pieces but not substantial quantities."
A holiday in much of Europe on Friday helped undermine London-traded futures, knocking March down to new contract lows.
The benchmark March contract slipped to a low of 946 stg a tonne but still failed to spark an upturn in industry buying.
Traders in Europe said the quantities of physical cocoa on offer were not substantial either. "I don't get the impression the origins are chasing this market lower," one said.

Origins such as Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Nigeria were in the market daily but selling pressure was not heavy. Cocoa was beginning to pile up at Ivorian ports but freight rates had yet to be settled and traders said cocoa would not be arriving in Amsterdam until the second half of November.
"It's starting to come down from up-country and from what I've heard the quality is good," one said.
Amsterdam warehouse sources said inventories were still high and throughput to Dutch processors was continuning apace.
But demand for cocoa products was also patchy.
Traders said chocolate manufacturers were in the market for butter but there was little sign of heavy buying ahead of the Christmas or Easter periods.
"They're basically filling the gaps they've got in their cover," said one. --Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
